description.full: Demons are malevolent supernatural entities found across virtually every world religion and culture. In Abrahamic traditions (Christianity, Islam, Judaism), demons are typically understood as fallen angels who rebelled against God or evil spirits that tempt and harm humanity. Eastern religions feature similar entities—Hindu Rakshasas, Buddhist Maras, Japanese Oni—though with varying characteristics and theological roles. Demonology, the systematic study of demons, encompasses their hierarchies, classifications, and behaviors. Historical demon beliefs have been invoked to explain mental illness, disease, misfortune, and moral failings. Demonic possession—the taking control of a human host by a demon—has been reported across cultures throughout history, leading to exorcism practices in multiple religious traditions. While demons are primarily theological and cultural concepts, belief in demonic entities remains strong in many religious communities worldwide. Reported encounters with demons continue to the present day. The study of demons intersects theology, psychology, anthropology, folklore, and the history of religion, raising profound questions about the nature of evil, consciousness, and belief.
